entities.name: 2019 Turkish offensive into north-eastern Syria
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The 2019 Turkish offensive into north-eastern Syria was a military operation launched by the Turkish military, in coordination with the Syrian National Army, against the Democratic Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria, a region in northeastern Syria that had declared autonomy from the Syrian government. The offensive began on October 9, 2019, and intensified on October 11, with the Turkish military advancing into the region and the Syrian National Army fighting against the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces. The operation was sparked by Turkey's long-standing concerns about the presence of Kurdish militants in the region and its desire to create a 30-kilometer buffer zone along the Syrian-Turkish border.

The offensive was carried out by the Turkish military, with air and artillery support, and involved the deployment of ground troops and tanks. The Syrian National Army, which was fighting alongside the Turkish military, was made up of Syrian rebels who had been supported by Turkey in the past. The operation resulted in the displacement of tens of thousands of people, including Kurds and other minority groups, who fled the region in fear of violence.

The 2019 Turkish offensive into north-eastern Syria had significant consequences for the region and the wider Middle East. It led to the creation of a new safe zone along the Syrian-Turkish border, which was established through a series of agreements between Turkey and the United States. The operation also marked a significant escalation of the conflict in Syria, which had been ongoing since 2011, and led to increased tensions between Turkey and the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces.
